recipes.name: Roasted Okra
ingredients_raw: 18 fresh okra pods, sliced 1/3 inch thick
2 teaspoons kosher salt, or to taste
2 teaspoons black pepper, or to taste

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C). Line a baking sheet with aluminum foil.
Arrange okra in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet. Drizzle with olive oil; sprinkle with kosher salt and pepper.
Roast in the preheated oven until okra is lightly browned and tender, 10 to 15 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Roasted Okra
raw_recipe.description: This roasted okra seasoned with olive oil, salt, and pepper is simple to make and turns out with a texture that is firm and toothsome, not gummy.

video.description: In this video, Nicole shows you three deliciously different ways to cook okra. These recipes use an air-fryer, oven, and stove to roast and fry the southern favorite veggie. To roast in the oven, place the prepared okra on a baking sheet and coat with oil before roasting. Air-frying the okra uses cooking spray, an egg coating, and cornmeal to crisp and cook the pods. Check out the video to see how to make these crispy southern sides!

review.reviewBody: I am originally from the Dominican Republic and just to give out a tiny little secret to getting rid of most of the sliminess of okras... If you place them in just enough cold water to cover and squeeze an entire lime into the water and lime juice and just let it sit for about 10-15 minutes, then drain and season to please, I promise it will lose most of the slimy texture you get when stewing, etc... Hope this helps :-)

Mercy me, these were delicious. I cut a few okra up, splashed a little olive oil in the bowl, sprinkled a little seasoning salt on them, tossed and spread in a pan along side sliced zucchini. I rarely fry foods, so this was a terrific substitute for fried okra. Keep in mind that the longer you cook it, the smaller it shrinks, so what you think will serve four could end up being barely enough for 2.

Excellent option for really tasty okra. Split the smaller ones 3 strips larger and placed in a mixing bowl.. Lined baking sheet with foil. Mixed olive oil, black pepper, Sriracha salt, old bay, minced garlic, onion flakes in a small bowl and spooned over okra and turned over gently. Spread on foil and sprinkled with grated Parmesan cheese. Cooked about 25 min till lightly brown and okra starts to get a lil’ wrinkly like my skin. Turned off the oven and let it stand in hot oven while pan frying ham steak. Served with black eyed peas. Okra was very zesty, firm, not slimy and definitely a keeper. This recipe can be altered a bazillion ways . No picture; got lost in the moment.

Absolutely fabulous way to prepare okra. Make sure your okra is young and not longer than 3 or 3.5 inches in length. Make sure you slice them exactly half an inch to 3/4 of an inch... any bigger and they are not roasted properly. I increased my roasting time to 30 minutes and roasted them at 430°. I used a very little bit of cayenne pepper to give it an extra sassy kick! Next time I plan to add a tablespoon of lemon juice pre cook. Oh, and I put the oil, salt and pepper in a gallon ziplock to evenly coat. I didn't use foil but Pam on cookie sheet and they came out great. Definitely a fabulous recipe

This recipe is perfect when you went the crispness of fried okra but not all the calories. My husbands Granny made fried okra often and he really enjoyed this recipe. I used the air fryer for 20 minutes, which I'll cut back a few minutes less next time, but boy it was as crispy as the really thing. Thanks for the recipe ncope

I used two bags of frozen cut okra. I tossed the okra with the oil and seasonings in a bowl before putting on the baking sheet. I cut the salt and pepper a bit and added garlic powder and a few flakes of red pepper. I roasted about 25 minutes and the okra was still tender but the slime was gone. This was easy and a winner for my crew.

Cut back on salt after reading the reviews. I added a little garlic and a bit of red pepper for kicks. Very good. I will use this again.

I also soaked the okra in 10-minutes in lemon juice because I didn't have lime. The okra wasn't slimey.

Yummy! Might like this better than traditional fried okra, and so easy to fix. I added 8 cherry tomatoes cut in half plus stirred in 1/4 cup Panko bread crumbs after reading several other recipes. Delicious.

This was so easy and delicious. Even my husband loved it! I followed another reviewer's advice and soaked the okra in water and lime juice for 15-20 minutes before slicing. The okra wasn't slimy at all.

Wonderful! Nice alternative to fried okra which is a staple here in the south. I have made this many times, the first several I followed exactly. Turned out fantastic. Since I have experimented and found it work well with larger pieces up to 1/2 inch. Works best with large okra. Never cook okra if it’s hard and woody, but the more tender large ones work well at 1/3”. Smaller okra including the very small most tender work at 1/2”
Or a little more. 

I have also experimented with the seasoning. A little salt and some Cajun seasoning like Tony’s (Cacheres) is our favorite. Season salt was good but we enjoyed a little heat from the Tony’s. Tony’s is good on everything!

You also have to experiment with your oven and temp. Mine seems to come out better closer to the element and at 450° rather than 435°. 

Good recipe.

I also am a "good Southern gardener" and right now have bucket loads of okra. I have just recently been trying other methods than breading and frying (my favorite). This recipe is now my second favorite. I did use garlic pepper (which has salt in it) and tossed instead of drizzling the olive oil. I found that at 15 min. it was still very soft and not browned at all. I ended up cooking about 30 min. If you want it browned and a little crunchy figure on doubling the cooking time. The end result was excellent and is much easier and less messy than frying. Thanks from another Southern okra lover!
Simple and delicious! Roasted up a batch, some was eaten as is, the rest added to a leftover vegetable soup! Will do again for me as hubs isn't a fan.
Perfect. simple. Made the okra browned and a bit crunchier. No sogginess and kept the okra flavor by not overpowering seasonings or oils. Must repeat
Don't use aluminum or other metals like Iron or lead when cooking Okra as it's used as a binder of metals.

I saw some very fresh okra and decided to buy it. Didn't want to boil . Instead I referred to the internet and the first thing that appeared in my search was roasted okra. It was easy and delicious, not slimy. I will never boil okra again
I added some cayenne garlic pepper flakes onion power. Real tasty
I added some "slap yo mama" seasoning to this and it was fabulous!

Used the ingredients but didn't measure anything. Friends have a great garden every year and gave a small amount... knowing that my husband only eats two veggies... Green beans and corn. I had plenty so had some for supper last night, been picking at the leftovers cold from the fridge this afternoon and will have the rest for supper tomorrow night. Thanks for the easy and delicious new way to make very good recipes
Picked from the garden - straight to the oven with this amazing recipe, and it was beyond delicious! I added my own sun-dried tomatoes for one of the best, light dinners I've ever eaten!
